slides.title: City Places
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 1 English, Unit 9: City Places. In this unit you will learn the words for places in a town — the shop, the market, the school, the hospital and the library. You will learn about the people who work in these places, and the words that tell us where something is: near, far and next to. You will meet the traffic lights too, and learn that red means stop and green means go. A town is full of helpful places and kind people, and we all help to keep it clean and safe. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name places in a town (shop, market, school, hospital, library, park).
Name some people who help us (teacher, doctor, shopkeeper).
Say where a place is using position words (near, next to, here, there).
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name places in a town (shop, market, school, hospital, library, park). You will also name some people who help us (teacher, doctor, shopkeeper). You will also say where a place is using position words (near, next to, here, there). Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: shop, market, school, hospital, library, park. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes A Walk Around Town and Talk about City Places. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: Say what is in your town
bullets: Name one place in your town. Say 'a' before most words, but 'an' before a vowel sound: a shop, an airport.
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Say what is in your town. Name one place in your town. Say 'a' before most words, but 'an' before a vowel sound: a shop, an airport. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 - Listen and point. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
